1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved by the applicants - Shyam Lal, Girish Kumar and Sakaturam seeking bail in Case No.890 of 2022 arising out of Case Crime No.1020 of 2018, under sections 420, 465, 468, 470, 471 I.P.C. & Section 3/7 Essential Commodities Act & Section 66D I.T. (Amendment) Act, 2000 & Section 34 of Aadhar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act 2016, Police Station Kotwali,
District Muzaffarnagar, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that co-accused Brijpal Singh, Sudesh Kumar and Pravin Kumar have been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in Criminal Misc.
Anticipatory Bail Application No.1019 of 2023 vide order dated 17.4.2023 and the case of the present applicants stands on similar footing.

It is also submitted that after investigation charge Shyam Lal And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141714047/
1 sheet has been submitted against the applicants, therefore, applicants are under apprehension of imminent arrest.

sentences.text: In case, the applicants are released on bail, they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record and the fact that other co-accused persons have already been enlarged on anticipatory bail and the case of the present applicants is on similar footing to that of aforesaid co-accused persons, therefore, the applicants are also entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
6.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that co-accused Brijpal Singh, Sudesh Kumar and Pravin Kumar have been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in Criminal Misc.
5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record and the fact that other co-accused persons have already been enlarged on anticipatory bail and the case of the present applicants is on similar footing to that of aforesaid co-accused persons, therefore, the applicants are also entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. opennyai_summary.decision:
Anticipatory Bail Application No.1019 of 2023 vide order dated 17.4.2023 and the case of the present applicants stands on similar footing.
In case, the applicants are released on bail, they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial.
The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
7. In the event of arrest of the applicants - Shyam Lal, Girish Kumar and Sakaturam, they shall be released on anticipatory bail during pendency of trial on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/-
with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the learned trial court unless exempted;
( ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
8. In default of any of the conditions, this bail order shall stand automatically vacated.
